title: Static factory methods that reuse instances

blocks.text: A **static factory method** is a static method that returns an instance, used instead of a public constructor. Unlike a constructor it has a name, and it may return an object that already exists rather than always making a new one.

items: `static Color of(int red, int green, int blue)`: each part is between `0` and `255`, both included. Anything else throws `IllegalArgumentException`.
`static Color fromHex(String hex)` reads `#RRGGBB` (upper or lower case), for example `#FF8000`.
Both factories hand out **one shared instance per distinct color**: asking again for the same parts returns the same object (`==`), not a new one.
No constructor is public: the factories are the only way in.

blocks.text:
Color.of(255, 128, 0).green()               -> 128
Color.fromHex("#ff8000") == Color.of(255, 128, 0) -> true
Color.of(256, 0, 0)                         -> IllegalArgumentException

cases.says: Color.of and Color.fromHex return colors with the requested red, green and blue parts.
Asking twice for the same parts, by either factory, returns the very same object.
A part below 0 or above 255 is refused with IllegalArgumentException.
Every constructor is private, so the factories are the only way to get a color.

concepts: A static factory method can be used instead of a constructor, and may return an existing instance.
